Lyngvig 1868, lost 1933) as a memorial to his parents Enevold Thygesen and Mariane · broellund.jermiinnielsen.dk, “Christiane Nielsdatters efterkommere” (Christiane Nielsdatter’s descendants) — the children of Søren Andersen Jensen and Larsine Larsen, among them Sørine Andrea, b. 21.6.1896
S56 A.K. Sørensen, the Enevoldsen family in Haurvig (rosenkilde.nu), based on parish registers and probate records — Christen Olesen Enevoldsen, b. Årgab 17.10.1871, drowned 1.4.1896, son of Enevold Jeppesen Enevoldsen (b. 10.1.1848) and Ane Iversen; Peder Enevoldsen, b. Haurvig 8.8.1870, son of the smallholder Christen Nielsen Enevoldsen and Karen Marie Nielsen
S57 Esbjerg City Archives, three negatives by the photographer Paul Bølling, Kongensgade 8, ordered by the Enevoldsen family, Rolfsgade 127 (arkiv.dk) — B21691 “Fest hos familien Enevoldsen, ca. 1944” (party at the Enevoldsen family’s, c. 1944), with the description “revisor Arne Enevoldsen (f. 1913) og hustruen Annegrethe (f. 1916)”; B24974 “Barselsseng, 1943-1945” (childbed); B24975 “Nyfødt i vugge, ca. 1944” (newborn in cradle), with the daughter, born in May 1944, and the remark “Ifølge kirkebogen skiftede Annette efternavn til Hyllested i 1954” (according to the parish register Annette changed her surname to Hyllested in 1954). The pictures were part of the exhibition “Fra vugge til grav — Paul Bølling billeder 1940-1960” (From cradle to grave), EBA 2004
S58 C. P. Eisenreich, clerk in the Lifeboat Service: “Det Nørrejydske Redningsvæsen — dets Tilblivelse, Organisation og Historie” (The North Jutland Lifeboat Service — its origin, organisation and history), E. Jespersens Forlag, Copenhagen 1927, published with a grant from the Carlsberg Foundation. The chapter on the Vedersø station, pp. 311—315: the station’s foundation in 1852 with a rocket apparatus from England in 1851, lifeboat and boathouse in 1854, rebuildings in 1879 and 1892, new boats in 1886 and 1924; the superintendents Chr. M. Stage (until 1864), Morten Th. Stage (1864—1908) and Poul Pedersen Bank (from 1908); the full list of rescue operations 1858—1925 with 300 rescued in all and 55 unsuccessful launches; and on p. 314 the entry with portrait: “Niels Silkjær blev ansat som Baadmand den 1. Januar 1879 og tog sin Afsked paa Grund af Alder den 1. Oktober 1916, og blev kort efter dekoreret med Dannebrogsmændenes Hæderstegn. Han har deltaget 7 Gange med Redningsbaaden og 8 Gange med Raketapparaterne i Redningen af 195 skibbrudne.” Digitisation: Library of the Danish Genealogical Society, slaegtsbibliotek.dk/2023/940039.pdf
S59 P. Storgaard Pedersen: “Ulfborg Herred — En historisk-topografisk Beskrivelse” (Ulfborg Hundred — a historical-topographical description), 1900 — on the farm name Silbjerg in Husby parish: “Gaarden Silbjerg, sydøst for Præstegaarden, bar formodentlig Navn af, at Skraaningen i gammel Tid har været bevokset med Pil, hvis ældre Navn var Silja.” (The farm Silbjerg, south-east of the rectory, presumably took its name from the slope having in olden times been overgrown with willow, whose older name was Silja.) Digitisation: ronlev.dk/bibliotek/2194.pdf
S60 Censuses for Husby parish, Ulfborg Hundred (Danish National Archives, digitised enumeration lists) — the census of 1850 lists Niels Jensen (Poulsgaard), Maren Jacobsdatter and Sidsel Cathrine Nielsdatter together in a house in Øe; the rest of the entry is difficult to decipher. The census of 1 February 1855 lists the household in Øe: Thomas Jensen, 30, smallholder and fisherman (“han lever mest ved Fiskerie”, he lives mostly by fishing), Anne Marie Jensen, 28, born in Vedersø parish, the pensioner Niels Jensen, 53, and his stepdaughter Sidsel Cathrine Nielsdatter, 35, who supports herself by spinning; Thomas Jensen listed in Øe in 1860 and 1870, without cadastral number, since the older lists do not give cadastral numbers; Niels Thomsen and his first wife Ane Johanne Kristensen listed in Øe in 1880 without cadastral number; Niels Thomsen Silkjær and Ane Jensen listed on cad. no. 13b in Øe in 1890, 1901 and 1911. The census of 1890 lists the household with the parents as “Niels Thomsen” and “Ane Jensen” and all five children with the farm name: Ane Marie, Thomas, Ane Johanne, Jens Klaus and Esper Nielsen Silkjær
S61 Ulfborg-Hind district court: land register for Husby parish, fol. 53 and 111 (cad. no. 13b, Cabinet F no. 464) and fol. 59 (cad. no. 13a), and land register for Vedersø parish, fol. 280 (cad. no. 44b) — titles, encumbrances and course of ownership, including the endorsement of allotment in January 1879, the sale in 1924, the titles of 1937 and 1952 and the reference to the name certificate (read with the year 1907). Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline
S62 Ulfborg-Hind district court: deed and mortgage book vol. 12, fol. 220 and 222 — deed of 16 February 1847, read in 1848 (the date read both as 29 March and as 29 October), from Thomas Miltersen Øe to his son Jens Thomsen for the farm in Øe, with a retirement-maintenance contract for Thomas Miltersen and Maren Madsdatter, charged on the whole of cad. no. 13
S63 Ulfborg-Hind district court: deed and mortgage book — deed of 19 June 1851 from Jens Thomsen “af Øe Bye” to Niels Jensen for parcel no. 2, cad. no. 13b, “beliggende i Øe i Husbye Sogn” — 200 rigsbankdaler, new hartkorn 1 skp. ¾ alb., divided in accordance with the Ministry of the Interior’s resolution of 24 May 1851; with the parcel went the previously registered right of retirement maintenance, witnessed by A. Salto and Peder Christian (surname uncertain); and deed of 18 December 1854, read 4 April 1855 (vol. 15, pp. 162—163), from Niels Jensen to Thomas Jensen of Husby: “et fritliggende Huus, der er beliggende i Silkjær og er Parcellen No. 2, Matr. No. 13b”
S64 Ulfborg-Hind district court: deed and mortgage book vol. 24, pp. 117—118 — deed of 2 August 1876 to “Thomas Jensen Silkjær i Husby” for cad. no. 44b in Vedersø parish; and the name certificate for Niels Thomsen for the name Niels Silkjær — the parish register’s endorsement at the baptism dates the certificate 21 November 1905, while the land register’s reference is read as 27 November 1907; the discrepancy has not been resolved
S65 Husby parish register, male births 1855 — Niels Thomsen, born 9 July 1855, baptised in church 22 July. The parents’ column reads “Hmd. Øekjær Thomas Jensen og Hustru Anne Marie Jansdatter, 28 Aar” (smallholder, Øekjær, Thomas Jensen and his wife Anne Marie Jansdatter, 28 years). Among the godparents Niels Poulsgaard and Johanne Cathrine (wife of the smallholder Jesper Jensen — Jesper and Esper are the same name), Kirstine Hansdatter (daughter of the smallholder Peder Jensen), the girl Ane Marie Jensdatter and the bachelor Ole Jensen, “alle af Husby” (all of Husby). In the margin the name Silkjær has been added “ifl. Bevis 21/11 1905” (according to certificate 21/11 1905). The godparent “Johanne Cathrine, wife of the smallholder Jesper Jensen” can be identified through the district’s genealogical records (1uz.dk) as Johanne Cathrine Jensdatter, born in Øe in 1824, married on 16 March 1851 in Husby Church to Esper Jensen Klit — Thomas Jensen’s brother, cf. S69 — whose children were born in Øe; she died in January 1856. The husband is in all likelihood the Esper Jensen Ø. who survived the wreck of 1878, cf. S66. Whether the marginal endorsement of the name certificate also gives the issuing authority or a journal number has not been read. The date 21 November 1905 falls between two schemes — access to name certificates from the authorities under the royal resolution of 26 May 1903 ended on 1 July 1905, and the Names Act of 1904 was only in practical use from 1906 — so the basis on which the certificate was issued is unresolved; the certificate file itself has not been examined. Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline
S66 Husby parish register, male deaths 1883, no. 7 — Jesper Jensen (Klit): died “formodentlig 17 Juni” (presumably 17 June), “inddrevet paa Fjaltring Strand d. 17 Juli” (washed ashore on Fjaltring beach on 17 July), buried 22 July in Husby churchyard; “2den Gang gift Huusmand, i Økjær og Fisker, født paa Husby Klit. Fader Jens Olesen” (twice-married smallholder, in Økjær, and fisherman, born on Husby Klit; father Jens Olesen), 54¼ years. The register’s collective note for nos. 7—11: “Disse 5 tilligemed Ungkarl Jeppe Jensen af Nørfjand forlod Land med Jørgen Sørensens Skib Natten mellem 15 og 16 Juni, men ere ikke senere komne i Land, hvorfor de maa ansees for at være druknede. Sidst ere de blevne sete 4—5 Mil fra Land Løverdag 16 Juni om Eftermiddagen af Fiskerne paa et andet Fiskerskib fra Vedersø Klit, da disse efter endt Gjerning, kort før en frembrydende Sydøststorm, søgte Land. Baaden er i kantret Tilstand set drivende ved Hanstholm.” (These 5, together with the bachelor Jeppe Jensen of Nørfjand, put out with Jørgen Sørensen’s boat in the night between 15 and 16 June, but have not since come ashore, and must therefore be considered drowned. They were last seen 4—5 miles from land on Saturday 16 June in the afternoon by the fishermen of another boat from Vedersø Klit, who, their work done, were making for land shortly before a south-easterly gale broke. The boat has been seen drifting capsized off Hanstholm.) The register’s “2den Gang gift” agrees with the genealogical database’s two marriages (1851 and 1856). Marriages, the wives’ names and the children’s birthplaces: genealogical database for the Sønder Nissum district, 1uz.dk. Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline
S67 Husby parish register, male deaths 1878 — collective note at the entries for the five drowned: “Disse 5 druknede paa Havet ud for Stagen i Vedersø [Sogn] Kl. 11 [Formiddag] d. 9 Novbr. De havde staaet paa Havet efter deres Kroge; men paa den inderste Revle fyldtes Baaden; og kun Formanden, Husmand og Fisker Esper Jensen Ø., kom levende i Land, reddet ved en Aare. Iver Chr. Olesen Kløves Lig kom ikke i Land.” (These 5 drowned at sea off Stagen in Vedersø [parish] at 11 [a.m.] on 9 November. They had been out at sea after their hooks; but on the innermost bar the boat filled; and only the foreman, smallholder and fisherman Esper Jensen Ø., came ashore alive, saved by an oar. Iver Chr. Olesen Kløve’s body did not come ashore.) Square brackets are supplied. The note singles out only Iver Chr. Olesen Kløve’s body as not having come ashore; by implication the other four, Thomas Jensen among them, came ashore and were buried. Note that the register writes “efter deres Kroge” (after their hooks), where the newspaper letter writes that the boat was fetching nets. Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline
S68 Vedersø parish register, marriages 1853, no. 6 (Arkivalieronline) — 20 November 1853, “I Kirken”: “Ungk. og Fisker Thomas Jensen af Husby Klit, 27¾ Aar gl., hjemme hos Broderen Ole Jensen ibid.” (bachelor and fisherman Thomas Jensen of Husby Klit, 27¾ years old, living with his brother Ole Jensen in the same place) and “Pigen Anne Marie Jansdatter af Tarpgaard, 26 Aar gl., hos Faderen Jan Andersen Tarpgaard, Gmd. i Vedersø” (the girl Anne Marie Jansdatter of Tarpgaard, 26 years old, with her father Jan Andersen Tarpgaard, farmer in Vedersø); witnesses Jan Andersen and Jens Olesen — the fathers of bride and groom
S69 Genealogical database for the Sønder Nissum district, 1uz.dk — the family of Jens Olufsen Klit (1785—1861) and Maren Thomasdatter (1790—1861): children born on Husby Klit, among them Ole Jensen (1818—1859), Thomas Jensen (born 12 December 1825, died 9 November 1878 at sea, married to Anne Marie Jansdatter Tarpgaard), Esper Jensen Klit (1829—1883) and Anne Marie Jensdatter Klit (b. 1837), married to Anders Knudsen Øe and later married twice more. The parents are identical with the family file’s Jens Olesen Klit and Maren Thomasdatter — the same years of baptism, the same days of death in March 1861. The naming confirms the line: Esper’s son of 1853 was called Jens Olesen Jespersen — after his paternal grandfather — and the daughter of 1857 by his second wife was given the name of his dead first wife, Johanne Cathrine. That the drowned beach bailiff Anders Knudsen Ø. is the sister’s husband rests on the coincidence of names and her later marriages; the database’s entries have not been checked against the original parish registers
S70 Nysogn parish register (Holmsland Klit), male births 1904 — Kristen Lauridsen Silkjær, born 4 May 1904 at Aargab, the mother the widow Kristiane Enevoldsen, Aargab, 31, Thomas Nielsen Silkjær as declared father. Godparents: the girl Sidsel Enevoldsen, Haurvig; farmer Simon Enevoldsen, Haurvig; fishery warden Enevold Jepsen Enevoldsen, Bjerregaard; bachelor Niels Christian Jespersen, Aargab. There is no corresponding entry among female births, and the entry does not refer to the child as a twin (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S71 Nysogn parish register (Holmsland Klit), marriages 1906 — 5 May 1906 in Haurvig Church: bachelor Thomas Nielsen Silkjær of Esbjerg, b. 10 January 1882 in Husby, son of the smallholder Niels Silkjær and his wife Ane Jensen, 24, and the widow Christiane Enevoldsen of Aargab, b. 27 March 1873 in Haurvig, daughter of the farmer Simon Enevoldsen and his wife Anne Marie Christensen, widow of the smallholder Christen Olesen Enevoldsen (d. 1 April 1896), 33. Marriage licence of 30 April and probate court certificate of 3 May 1906. Witnesses: fishery warden Enevold Jepsen Enevoldsen, Bjerregaard, and farmer Simon Enevoldsen, Haurvig. The sources alternate between the spellings Olsen and Olesen; Olesen is used here (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S72 Levy rolls, 5th conscription area (Danish National Archives) — Husby, levy district 28, serial no. 2: “Thomas Nielsen Silkjær”, father “Hmd. og Fisker Niels Thomsen” (smallholder and fisherman Niels Thomsen), born in Husby 10/1 1882, removal reference 4-33a-D-160. Esbjerg, levy district 33a, letter D (1906), no. 160: branch Navy, reported 21/9 1905, discharged 23/4 1906; the endorsements “28/9 03. Søfbog.”, “U. A. 1905” and arrival from 5.28 on 21/5 1906 on a removal certificate of 12/5 1906. Levy district 36 (Holmsland Klit according to the key to the levy rolls), letter H (1910), no. 17: “Fra 4-33a-D-160”, recalled 23/10—30/10 1910. “E.K.” stands for actual military service. Note the forms of name: the son is entered as Silkjær, the father as Thomsen
S73 Husby parish register, confirmations 1896 — “Thomas Nielsen Silkjær af Økjær”, parents “Husmd. … og Fisker Niels Thomsen (kaldt Silkjær) og Hustru Anna Jensen” (smallholder … and fisherman Niels Thomsen (called Silkjær) and his wife Anna Jensen), born in Husby parish 10 January 1882, baptised 5 February the same year; marks g and mg (good and very good) for knowledge and conduct (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S74 Census of 1 February 1901, Vedersø parish, Ulfborg-Hind Hundred, Ringkøbing County — main list for cad. no. 67 at Klit By, the household of Peder Sand Pedersen; on the tenth line “Tomas Nielsen Silkær”, male, born 10 January 1882, unmarried, National Church, birthplace Husby, farmhand (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S75 Esbjerg parish register, marriages 19 September 1916, by Pastor Roesen — “Pige Christine Oline Enevoldsen, Helgolandsgade 14, Esbjerg, født Holmslands Klit, Ny Sogn den 17 May 1896, Datter af afd. Fisker Christen Olesen Enevoldsen og Hustru Kristiane Enevoldsen, Esbjerg” (the girl Christine Oline Enevoldsen, Helgolandsgade 14, Esbjerg, born on Holmsland Klit, Nysogn, on 17 May 1896, daughter of the late fisherman Christen Olesen Enevoldsen and his wife Kristiane Enevoldsen, Esbjerg) and “Ungkarl, Fisker, Niels Peder Edvard Nielsen, Esbjerg, født i Esbjerg den 3. Oktober 1894, Søn af Fisker Jens Højberg Nielsen og Hustru Jensine f. Jensen, Esbjerg” (bachelor, fisherman, Niels Peder Edvard Nielsen, Esbjerg, born in Esbjerg on 3 October 1894, son of the fisherman Jens Højberg Nielsen and his wife Jensine née Jensen, Esbjerg); witnesses the fisherman Jens Højberg Nielsen, Esbjerg, and the fisherman Enevold J. Enevoldsen, Esbjerg. In the margin: “Navneforandring ifl. kgl. Bevilling af 16 September 1930: Niels Peder Edvard Højberg” (change of name by royal licence of 16 September 1930) (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S76 Census of 1 February 1916, Esbjerg — Hjertinggade 13, household 7946: Thomas Silkjær, head of household, fisherman; Kristiane Silkjær, housewife; and under Children: Kristian, Anna, Niels, Arne and Ejlert, all with the surname Silkjær. The same census: Helgolandsgade 14 with households 1376 (Jens Højberg Nielsen, b. 1862, with his wife Jensine and the sons Jens Højberg, Krester Højberg and Harry) and 10655 (Hansen) — neither Kristine Oline nor the groom appears in either of them; the property held several households. At Gl. Færgevej 7 there is no Silkjær household in 1916. Three of the seven years of birth in the Hjertinggade household differ by one year from the parish registers’; cf. caveat 23 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S77 Census of 1 February 1916, Nysogn, Hind Hundred — Enevold Jepsen Enevoldsen, b. 1848, and Ane Iversen as a household of two; Kristine Oline Enevoldsen is not in the household (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S78 Census of 1 February 1921, Esbjerg — Helgolandsgade 14, first floor, flat 2, household 4238: Niels Peder E. Nielsen (3/10 1894, married, born Esbjerg), Kristine Oline Nielsen (17/5 1896, married, born Holmsland Klit) and Gerda Jensine H. Nielsen (23/2 1917, born Esbjerg). The columns for moving in are struck through for the husband and the daughter, who were both born in Esbjerg; for her they are filled in: moved in 1916, from Holmsland (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S79 Census of November 1940, Esbjerg — Niels Peder Edvard Højberg, fisherman, in a household with his daughter Gerda, b. 23 February 1917, and two lodgers; no wife in the household — Kristine Oline had died in May the same year, cf. S83. Among the lodgers Kaj Bøndergaard, b. 25.8.1920 — the date of birth matches the family file’s Kaj, Karen Marie Silkjær’s son (chapter 20); a young fisherman lodging with an older fisherman shows that the two circles touched, not why (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S80 Death entry 1923, Esbjerg — Enevold Jepsen Enevoldsen, b. 1848, died at Helgolandsgade 14, 75 years old; he does not appear at the address in the census of 1921 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S81 Census of 1925, Esbjerg — Helgolandsgade 14: Niels Peder E. Nielsen, Kristine Oline Nielsen and their daughter, here written out in full as “Gerda Jensine Højbjerg” — the household of 1921 still together (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S82 Census of 5 November 1930, Esbjerg — Cort Adelersgade 15b: Kristine Oline appears in the household, 34 years old — her last appearance in the censuses (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S83 Death certificate issued by a doctor, form B.1 (Form. no. 18a) — Danish National Archives, death certificates, Jutland, Ribe towns 1940. “Højberg, Kristine Oline. gift.” (married) Born 17-5-96 at Aargab. Position and occupation: “gift med Fisker” (married to a fisherman). Residence: Frodesgade 149, population-register municipality Esbjerg. Place of death: Esbjerg Municipal Hospital. Date of death: 18-5 1940 at 3.05. Principal illness (column 7): “C. uteri”, complication “Kakeksia”. Immediate cause of death (column 8): in Danish “Hjertesvækkelse” (heart failure), in Latin “Paresis cordis”. Certain signs of death: rigor mortis, livor mortis. Attending and examining doctor: Esbjerg Municipal Hospital, Surgical Department, by Jakob Bak, post-mortem examination 18-5 1940 at 9.30. The fields for entry in the parish register and for the committal are not filled in. The transcript in the Register of Deaths (Danish Genealogical Society, dodsregister.dk, from the Danish National Archives’ transcription portal) gives column 8 only
S84 Zion parish register, Esbjerg, female deaths 1940 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — “Christine Oline Højberg f. Enevoldsen”, died 18 May 1940 at Esbjerg Municipal Hospital, buried 22 May 1940 in Esbjerg New Cemetery by Pastor Birke, 44 years. The entry reads: “Gift med Fisker af Frodesgade 149. F. i Aargab Holmsland Klit Sogn 17 Maj 1896 som Dt. af Fisker Christen Olesen Enevoldsen og Hustru Kristiane f. Enevoldsen” (married to a fisherman of Frodesgade 149; born at Aargab, Holmsland Klit parish, 17 May 1896, daughter of the fisherman Christen Olesen Enevoldsen and his wife Kristiane née Enevoldsen), married to Niels Peder Edvard Højberg
S85 Zion parish register, Esbjerg, marriages 1940, no. 21 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — 11 May 1940, married by Pastor Bentzen in Zion’s Church: “Ungkarl Revisor Arne Enevoldsen, Havnegade 179. F. paa Holmslands Klit 26 Maj 1913 som Søn af Christine Oline Enevoldsen, Frodesgade 149” (bachelor, accountant, Arne Enevoldsen, Havnegade 179; born on Holmsland Klit 26 May 1913, son of Christine Oline Enevoldsen, Frodesgade 149) and “Pige Tandtekniker Annagrethe Thomsen, Nørrebrogade 26 Boldesager, Jerne S. F. 4. April 1916 som Dt. af Toldassistent Emil Peter Thomsen og Hustru Anna Agnete Gregersen s. St.” (the girl Annagrethe Thomsen, dental technician, Nørrebrogade 26, Boldesager, Jerne parish; born 4 April 1916, daughter of the customs assistant Emil Peter Thomsen and his wife Anna Agnete Gregersen of the same place). Witnesses: the bride’s father and “Fiskeskipper Silkjær, Havnegade 179”. Banns read on 21 April 1940 in Jerne Church, certificate of banns of 6 May 1940 from the parish priest of Jerne, reported to Jerne 14.5.1940. The father’s occupation and a few words in the bride’s column are read from the context
S86 Statstidende, deaths, as given in the Register of Deaths (Danish Genealogical Society, dodsregister.dk) — Ronald Søren Hyllested, b. 11 September 1916, d. 22 July 2004, last address Kongensgade 72, 2nd floor, 6700 Esbjerg; Annagrethe Hyllested, b. 4 April 1916, d. 21 December 2004, same address. The date of birth 4.4.1916 is identical with the bride’s in the marriage entry of 1940, cf. S85. The marriage between the two has since been read in Esbjerg’s civil marriage register, cf. S139. The same register, search on the surname Silkjær: Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, b. 10.1.1882, d. 20.3.1950, Esbjerg · Christiane Silkjær, b. 27.3.1873, d. 31.7.1963, Esbjerg town · Anna Silkjær, b. 17.2.1907, d. 10.10.1952, Esbjerg · Ane Kirstine Silkjær, b. 10.9.1910, d. 30.3.1969, last residence Guldager, Esbjerg medical district · Ane Marie Nielsen Silkjær, married name Lauridsen, b. 2.3.1880, d. 26.3.1960, Ringkøbing medical district · Ane Johanne, married name Madsen, b. 22.10.1883, d. 19.11.1956, Bølling Nørre Herred medical district · Jens Klaus Nielsen Silkjær, b. 6.5.1886, d. 25.7.1959, Rougsø medical district · Bodil Marie Silkjær, b. 8.4.1887, d. 13.7.1969, Mariager medical district · Esper Nielsen Silkjær, b. 17.3.1888, d. 1.12.1960, Struer · Jensine Kristine, married name Nørfjand, b. 17.12.1896, d. 23.2.1964, Ringkøbing medical district · Oluf Christian Silkjær, b. 25.1.1920, d. 21.4.2005. The register independently confirms the year of birth 1896 for Jensine Kristine, where the family file has 1897. Niels and Ejlert are not found under this spelling; the family file lists them as Silkær, and a search on that form has not been made
S87 Ringkjøbing Courthouse and Gaol: punishment register for Ringkjøbing Gaol 1871—1919, entry 1913 no. 40 (Danish National Archives, Regional Archives for North Jutland) — “Huusmand og Fisker Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, f. 10/1 1882 i Husby” (smallholder and fisherman Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, b. 10/1 1882 in Husby), with reference to case no. 29/13 and the offence given as “Blodskam” (incest). The sentence: “Forbedringshusarbejde i 18 Maaneder. Fra 27/4 1913 Kl. 8 Fm. paabegyndt Afsoning” (hard labour in the house of correction for 18 months; sentence begun 27/4 1913 at 8 a.m.). Delivered to Vridsløselille Prison on 2 July 1913 — the Vridsløselille register records him as admitted the following day, which corresponds to the travelling time. The entry bears his own signature
S88 Zion South parish register, Esbjerg, confirmations 24 April 1927 — Arne Enevoldsen, Færgevej 7, born Holmsland Klit 26.5.1913, baptised 15.6.1913 in Haurvig Church, confirmed by Pastor Bentzen. The father’s three columns are blank; the mother is entered as “Christine Oline Enevoldsen, Ugift 17-årig pige” (unmarried 17-year-old girl), and the remark reads “Udlagt barnefar: Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, 31 år” (declared father: Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, 31 years). The ages are the mother’s and father’s at the birth in 1913, not at the confirmation — the entry is copied from the baptismal certificate from Nysogn
S89 Esbjerg Municipality’s printed tax books 1892—1956 (database, Esbjerg City Archives) — A. Enevoldsen: office trainee, Havnegade 179, 1932 (21 kr., serial no. 33944, entered immediately after T. N. Silkjær, fishing skipper, same address, serial no. 33943; the house number is keyed as 175 in 1932 and as 169 in 1946 — see caveat 26) · clerk, Havnegade 179, 1935 (16 kr.) · accountant, Havnegade 179, 1939 (247 kr.) · accountant, Rolfsgade 127, 1941, 1943 (719 kr.) and 1946 (1174 kr.) · accountant, Gl. Vardevej 5, 1949 · accountant, Strandbygade 39, 1951 · accountant, Strandbygade 90a, 1956 (1681 kr.). The books give only an initial; the identification rests on the two addresses documented as his in other sources — Havnegade 179 in the marriage of 1940 and Rolfsgade 127 in the marriage of 1943, the census of 1940 and the Bølling negatives — on his being entered in 1932 immediately after his father at the same address, and on the sequence being unbroken: in no year do two A. Enevoldsens appear with the occupation of accountant. The books also list A. Enevoldsen, Mrs, Rolfsgade 127, 1949 (1045 kr.) — the former shared address, while Arne the same year appears at Gl. Vardevej 5; and N. P. Højbjerg, fisherman, Cort Adlersgade 15b, 1932 (70 kr.), the same address the census of 1930 gives for Kristine Oline and her husband. The series ends in 1956
S90 Kraks Vejviser (directory), Esbjerg, trade section Auditing — “Regnskabs-Kontoret, Arne Enevoldsen, Ny Havn, tlf. 2143”, 1941; the same entry without a personal name in 1944 and 1950. The Jydsk Telefon subscriber list of 1941 lists no. 2143 as “Arne, Revisor, Ny Havn”; in 1951 the same number and address stand under H. Meldgaard, accountant. The firm name Regnskabs-Kontoret (the Accounts Office) is found in Krak until at least 1978 and therefore says nothing about Arne’s connection after 1944. Advertisement in the Arbejdersamariternes Juleblad (the Workers’ Samaritans’ Christmas magazine) 1944: “Bogføring · Revision · Regnskabskontoret · Revisor Arne Enevoldsen . M. L. R. · Telefon 2143” (Bookkeeping · Auditing · the Accounts Office · accountant Arne Enevoldsen, M. L. R.). The abbreviation M. L. R. is a membership designation whose association has not been identified
S91 Vor Frelser parish register, Esbjerg, marriages 21 December 1943, fol. 157 no. 126 — the manager Thomas Kaj Nielsen (b. 9.9.1914, Skanderup parish) and Tove Siim, née Andersen (b. 19.3.1922, Grenaa), married by the parish priest P. Bentzen, Zion’s Church. Witnesses: “Revisor Arne Enevoldsen, Rolfsgade 127, Esbjerg” and the groom’s father
S92 Vedersø parish register, female births 1827, no. 6 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — Anna Marie Jansdatter Tarpgaard, born 25 September 1827, baptised at home the same day and presented in church on 4 November. Parents: the farmer Jan Andersen and his wife at Tarpgaard. The entry is the only contemporary source for her birthday; the census of 1855 (28 years) and the register of deaths of 1863 (36 years) both give an age one year too high
S93 Zion North parish register, Esbjerg, births 1944, serial no. 70, fol. 162 — the baptismal entry for the daughter Annette, born in May 1944; in the margin an endorsement of adoption by royal licence of 22 March 1954: Enevoldsen struck through, Hyllested written instead
S94 Esbjerg Municipality’s printed tax books 1892—1956 (database, Esbjerg City Archives), the family’s entries. T. N. Silkjær: fisherman, entered on the vessel “Robert Skov” without house number, 1905 (41.08 kr.) · fisherman, Gl. Færgevej 7, 1922 (entered as “Th”, 203 kr.), 1925, 1928 (“Th. N”) and 1930 · fishing skipper, Havnegade 179, 1932 (73 kr.) up to and including 1949. K. Silkjær, Mrs, Havnegade 179, 1951. A. Silkjær — two women, told apart by the occupation field: widow, Gl. Færgevej 7, 1930, widow, Havnegade 179, 1932, old-age pensioner at the same address 1935 (Ane Jensen) · sewing apprentice, Gl. Færgevej 7, 1928 and 1930, domestic help 1932, shop assistant, Havnegade 179, 1935—1951 (Anna). E. E. Silkjær, Miss, Havnegade 179, 1939 and 1941 (Elna Elisabeth, b. 1919) — no entries thereafter. E. M. Silkjær: share fisherman, Havnegade 179, 1932, 1935, 1941, 1943, 1946, 1949 and 1951, entered as fisherman in 1939 — fishing skipper only in 1954 and 1956, when he is the only Silkjær left at the address. Neither K. nor A. Silkjær has entries after 1951. N. Silkjær: fisherman, Gl. Færgevej 7, 1928 and 1930 · Knudsgade 18, 1932 · Hjertinggade 9, 1935 · Gormsgade 122, 1939, 1941 and 1943 · Strandbygade 67, 1946, 1949 and 1951. Also N. Silkjær, old-age pensioner, Peder Skramsgade 2, 1928 — Niels Thomsen Silkjær in his own home, the year he died; the address is confirmed by the census of 1925 [S96]. C. L. / K. L. Silkjær — the same man under both spellings, never in the same year: fisherman, Gl. Færgevej 7, 1925 (K. L.), 1928 and 1930 (C. L.) · Havnegade 179, 1932 (C. L.), share fisherman 1935, fisherman 1939, 1941 and 1943, share fisherman 1946, 1949 and 1951 (all K. L.) · fishing skipper, Spangsbergsgade 51, 1954 and 1956. The sequence is unbroken through all the database’s years 1925—1956. Also O. Silkjær, apprentice, Gl. Vardevej 78, 1954 — unidentified. C. Torbensen: Havnegade 132, 1922—1943, entered as fisherman, in 1932 and 1935 as share fisherman and in 1943 as fishing skipper · Rolfsgade 157, 1946—1956. T. E. Silkjær, chief clerk, Finsensgade 9, 1941 · Strandbygade 70, 1943, 1946, 1949, 1951, 1954 and 1956 — Tage Ewald Silkjær from Djursland, see chapter 19 [S97]. The house numbers 175 (1932) and 169 (1946) are read as keying errors for 179, see caveat 26
S95 Census of 5 November 1940, Esbjerg — Gormsgade 122: the household is entered under the surname Silkjær with the first names Niels, Ane Kirstine, Jørgen Georg and Elisabeth. The form’s columns for position in the household are not reproduced in the page consulted (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline). The same census, Havnegade 179: Ejlerth Marius Silkjær and his wife Dagmar, née Lodberg, as a household of their own with a single lodger; the form gives the wedding date as 24 September 1939
S96 Census of 5 November 1925, Esbjerg — Peder Skramsgade 2 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline): Silkjær, Niels, M, born 9/7 1855 in Husby, Danish, married · Ane, F, born 29/4 1858 in Ejsing, housewife · Poulsen, Niels, M, born 29/4 1917 in Husby, unmarried, entered as foster son. The dates of birth correspond to the parish registers for Niels Thomsen Silkjær and Ane Jensen; Landtingmark, which the family file gives as her birthplace, lies in Ejsing parish. The address is not found again in the census of 1930
S97 Census of 5 November 1940, Esbjerg — Finsensgade 9 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline): “Silkjær, Tage Ewald”, male, born 8/10 1917 in Ø. Alling, unmarried, entered as lodger and with the position of chief clerk in the bicycle and radio trade. The head of the household is the wholesaler Alfred Christian Nielsen in the same trade. Date and parish of birth correspond to Jens Klaus Nielsen Silkjær’s fourth son, born at Oustrup in Øster Alling parish
S98 Esbjerg City Archives, company database (ebasoeg.esbjerg.dk), entry no. 59, “Tropil (sodavands/mineralfabrik)” (soft-drinks/mineral-water factory) — author JDR, dated 26 July 2001, after a paper by Keld Lauge Jensen, Varde, 1979; reproduced on kimbj.dk. The Tropil mineral-water factory, Esbjerg 1934—1969, founded by Villy Bratborg (1901—1978) at Kongensgade 8, from 1936 Kronprinsensgade 15, from 1947 Møllegården in Gammelby. Sold on 1 October 1961 to the sales representative Tage E. Silkjær, “født i oktober 1917 på Randers-egnen” (born in October 1917 in the Randers area), a trained salesman formerly employed by, among others, Esbjerg Cykellager and Nellemann in Aarhus. The factory moved to Randersvej 8 on 1 October 1964 and closed on 24 February 1969
S99 Vor Frelser parish register, Esbjerg, marriages 19 July 1942, fol. 111, serial no. 59 (transcribed, Esbjerg City Archives, id 3975) — the bachelor and police constable Ronald Søren Hyllested, b. 11.9.1916 in Aarhus Cathedral parish, Teglværksgade 65, son of the coachman Henning Schortan Nielsen and Meta Kirstine Rasmussen Østersø, Aarhus, married to the young woman Ane Marie Villemoes, b. 25.1.1915 in Esbjerg, Teglværksgade 55, daughter of the machine manufacturer Jens Villemoes and Anine Cathrine Andreasen. Witnesses: the bride’s father and the groom’s father. Married by Pastor Gaub. Esbjerg’s tax books list him as police constable in 1941 (Kirkegade 62), 1943 and 1946 (Teglværksgade 65), 1949 (Jernbanegade 2) and 1951 (Kirkegade 101) — and as sales representative in 1954 and 1956 (Kirkegade 101), the same title used by the royal licence of 22 March 1954
S100 Samlerringen no. 1, February 1981 — short history of the Tropil mineral-water factory, Esbjerg: founded in 1934 by Villy Bratborg after nine years in America, new premises in 1936, a farm in Gammelby from 1947, in the mid-fifties c. 1 million bottles a year with a bottling capacity of 1,500 bottles an hour. “Da produktionen i 1961 var faldet til 1/3 af hvad den var i 50´erne” (when production in 1961 had fallen to a third of what it was in the fifties) Bratborg sold to “Tage Silkjær, en representant fra Randersegnen” (a representative from the Randers area), who “introducerede en ny sodavand” (introduced a new soft drink) — sales rose again to c. 1 million bottles in the late sixties. New factory building 1964, factory closed 1969. The account is independent of, but essentially consistent with, the archive’s text [S98]; neither names the new soft drink. Tropil’s range of labels is reproduced in Kims Øletiketter, kimbj.dk
S101 Elna Elisabeth Silkjær (20.1.1919—5.2.2015) — transcribed parish registers and censuses, Esbjerg City Archives. Born in Zion parish, baptised in Zion’s Church on 9 February 1919; parents the fishing skipper Thomas Nielsen Silkjær and his wife Kristiane Enevoldsen. Census 1925 (id 5099): Gammel Færgevej 7, front house, child in the household — the owner’s name entered as “Th. Silkjær”. Confirmed on 2 April 1933 in Zion North, fol. 209 no. 21, residence Havnegade 179, by Pastor Bentzen (id 9245). Married on 10 October 1942 in Zion South, fol. 147 no. 24 (id 546), as an office assistant, Havnegade 179, to the bachelor and clerk Holger Nielsen, b. 5.6.1919 in Esbjerg, Strandbygade 16, son of the late master tailor Anton Peder Nielsen and Maren Kathrine Vestergaard; witnesses the groom’s mother and the bride’s father. The son Kjeld Silkjær Nielsen born in March 1945 at St Joseph’s Hospital, baptised on 22 April in Zion North, fol. 227 no. 44 (id 3517); godparents among others Miss Anna Silkjær, shop assistant, Havnegade 179, and the fishing skipper Thomas Silkjær, Havnegade 179. The baptismal entry in the original (Zion parish, births 1919): born 20 January, birthplace Gl. Færgevej 7, the father entered as “Fisker Thomas Nielsen Silkjær” (fisherman), the mother as “Hustru Kristiane f. Enevoldsen, 45 Aar” (wife Kristiane née Enevoldsen, 45 years), with reference to the marriage in Haurvig on 5 May 1906; baptised in church on 9 February 1919 by Pastor Roesen. Four godparents, two of whom are the parents themselves: 1) the servant girl Christine Silkjær, Gl. Færgevej 7 — a Silkjær woman in service in the household, not identified; among Thomas’ sisters, Ane Kirstine (b. 1892, married on New Year’s Day 1920 to Christen Torbensen in Esbjerg) and Jensine Kristine (b. 1896) were both unmarried and of the right age. The census of 1 February 1921 lists no Christine at Gl. Færgevej 7. Ane Kirstine is the less likely of the two: the marriage entry of 1 January 1920 lists her as “tjenestepige i Haurvig” (servant girl in Haurvig), not in Esbjerg. Jensine Kristine is the more likely: in April 1917 she had a son outside marriage, whom her parents took in, and a twenty-year-old mother without a home of her own would indeed have had to go into service [S105]. The question nevertheless remains open. [S103] 2) the mother. 3) the labourer Christen Bøndergaard, Husby — the surname is also the one her sister Karen Marie married into in Husby Church in 1913, but the first name does not match her husband Kristian Kornelius. 4) the father. Death notice: “Elna Elisabeth Nielsen, født Silkjær, * 20. januar 1919, † 5. februar 2015”, fell asleep at Fanø Care Centre, buried from Gormsgade Chapel on 14 February
S102 Esbjerg’s burial registers 1884—1999, day journal for all the cemeteries 1967—1983, vol. 52 (transcribed, Esbjerg City Archives, id 17110) — Ane Kirstine Silkjær, née Hansen, born 10 September 1910, died 30 March 1969, buried 3 April 1969 in Fourfeldt Cemetery, section D 2, row 9, no. 1, the grave renewed until 31 December 1989. Identified as Niels Silkjær’s wife: name and year of birth correspond to the Ane Kirstine whom the census of 1940 lists in his household at Gormsgade 122, she bears the Silkjær name by marriage, and the cemetery is the one where Niels and Ejlert were buried in 1985. The marriage has not been traced
S103 Nysogn parish register, Holmsland Klit, marriages 1 January 1920 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — “Ungkarl Christen Tarbensen, f. i Haurvig 2. Marts 1896, Fisker i Haurvig” (bachelor Christen Tarbensen, b. in Haurvig 2 March 1896, fisherman in Haurvig), son of the farmer Christen Fjord Tarbensen and his wife Ane Kirstine Jensen of Haurvig, married to “Pigen Ane Kirstine Nielsen Silkjær, f. i Husby 3. September 1892, Tjenestepige i Haurvig” (the girl Ane Kirstine Nielsen Silkjær, b. in Husby 3 September 1892, servant girl in Haurvig), daughter of “Hmd. Niels Silkjær og Hustru Ane Jensen af Husby”. Witnesses: both fathers. Banns read on 14, 21 and 28 December 1919; married in church. The entry is the source that records the father under the name Silkjær in the parish’s own book, and it lists the bride as a servant girl in Haurvig — not in Esbjerg
S104 Vor Frelser parish register, Esbjerg, births 1907, serial no. 34 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — “Anna Silkær”, born in February 1907, birthplace “Esbjerg — Helgolandsgade 22”, baptised in church on 10 March 1907 by Pastor Berg. Parents: “Fisker Thomas Nielsen Silkær og Christiane Enevoldsen”, with reference to the marriage “Holmslandsklit 5/5-06”. Godparents: 1) the wife of the smallholder Niels Silkær, Husby · 2) the fisherman Georg Gaardestrup Thellefsen · 3) and his wife · 4) the smallholder Niels Silkær, Husby. Nos. 2 and 3 are bracketed together in the entry; the surname Thellefsen stands on the second line and in all likelihood applies to both. So half of the godparents are the child’s paternal grandparents from Husby, while no one from the mother’s Enevoldsen family on Holmsland Klit is included. Georg Gaardestrup Thellefsen has not been identified. The day of birth in February has not been read with certainty. The entry is the oldest known address of the family in Esbjerg and spells the name Silkær throughout
S105 Husby parish register, male births 1917, serial no. 6 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — “Niels Poulsen”, born 28 April 1917 in Økjær, Husby parish, Ulfborg Hundred. The mother: “Ugift Jensine Kristine Nielsen Silkjær, 20 Aar” (unmarried Jensine Kristine Nielsen Silkjær, 20 years). Declared father: “Tjenestekarl Laurits Nikolaj Poulsen, 22 Aar, Gudum” (farmhand Laurits Nikolaj Poulsen, 22 years, Gudum). Baptised in church on Whit Sunday, 27 May 1917, by the parish priest; “Pige Ane Kirstine Nielsen Silkjær” carried the child. Godparents: smallholder and fisherman Niels Silkjær · smallholder Ole Jensen Pedersen and his wife Ane Jensen, Røjkjær — “alle af Øe i Husby” (all of Øe in Husby). The entry makes the boy the daughter’s son of Niels Thomsen Silkjær and Ane Jensen and explains the entry “foster son” in the census of 1925. The census gives the birthday as 29 April; the parish register has the 28th.
S106 Census of 5 November 1930, Sønder Nissum parish — Fjand: the household of Martin Jeppesen Nørfjand, Jensine Kristine, the son Evald and Niels Poulsen, 13 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline). Compared with the census of 1925, the boy moves from his grandparents’ household in Esbjerg to his mother’s in Fjand between November 1925 and November 1930; Niels Thomsen Silkjær died on 17 June 1928, and his widow appears in the tax book of 1930 at Gl. Færgevej 7 with her son Thomas. The date of the marriage has not been traced, but it lies before the birth of the son Evald in 1927
S107 Sønder Nissum parish register, births 1927 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — Evald Jeppesen Nørfjand, born 10 November 1927 at 9.30 at Pilgaardhus, Sønder Nissum parish, Ulfborg Hundred; parents “Arbejdsmand Martin Jeppesen Nørfjand (10-8-94) og Hustru Jensine Kristine Nielsen Silkjær (17-12-96)” (labourer Martin Jeppesen Nørfjand and his wife Jensine Kristine Nielsen Silkjær). Godparents: Petrea Simonsen, wife of the smallholder Jens Nicolaisen · bachelor Jens Ingvart Jeppesen Nørfjand · bachelor Karl Marinus Jeppesen Nørfjand, all of Sønder Nissum.
