The entry lists the mother as wife but does not give the date of the marriage — this parish’s form records the parents’ dates of birth, not the marriage
S108 Esbjerg’s burial registers 1884—1999, day journals for all the cemeteries (transcribed, Esbjerg City Archives). Thomas Nielsen Silkjær, died 20.3.1950, 68 years, buried 24.3. — Gormsgade, section Ø, row 11, no. 9, note “D.D. (Dobbelt Dybde)” (double depth), renewed until 31.12.1970 (vol. 51, id 353). Christiane Silkjær, née Enevoldsen, b. 27.3.1873, died 31.7.1963, 90 years, buried 4.8. — the same grave, Gormsgade Ø-11-9, renewed until 31.12.1983 (vol. 51, id 3029). Ejlert Marius Silkjær, b. 29.1.1915, died 28.5.1985, buried 1.6. — Fovrfeld Cemetery, section B, row 2, no. 23 (vol. 53, id 27026). Niels Silkjær, b. 26.9.1910, died 16.4.1986, buried 19.4. — Fovrfeld Cemetery, section D 2, row 9, no. 2 (vol. 53, id 27131), next to his wife Ane Kirstine in no. 1 [S102]. Christen Fjord Silkjær Torbensen, b. 28.9.1921, died 30.11.1985, buried 5.12. — Gormsgade, section N, row 19, no. 14 (vol. 53, id 24923); the family file gives the year of birth as 1920, the register 1921 — the chronicle follows the register. Karen Marie Silkjær, née Schmidt, b. 9.9.1917, died 12.1.1973, buried 17.1. — Fourfeldt Cemetery, section D2, row 8, no. 35 (vol. 52, id 17929) — Tage Ewald Silkjær’s wife; she was born a month before him. The register gives the cemetery as “Gormsgade”, where the older parish registers write Esbjerg New Cemetery: it is the same cemetery under two names, and the chronicle uses the present one
S109 Vor Frelser parish register, Esbjerg, births 1931, fol. 76, serial no. 112 (transcribed, Esbjerg City Archives, id 7630) — Jørgen Georg Silkjær, born 25 August 1931 at Knudsgade 18, baptised on 6 September in Vor Frelsers Church by Dean Kjærgaard. The father Niels Silkjær, b. 26.9.1910; the mother Ane Kirstine Hansen, b. 10.9.1910, 20 years. Remark: “Forældrene viet i Vor Frelsers Kirke, Esbjerg, den 21-12-1930” (the parents married in Vor Frelsers Church, Esbjerg, on 21-12-1930). Godparents: the clerk Mette Hansen, Bag Teglværket 8 · the fishing skipper Thomas Silkjær, Gl. Færgevej · Mrs Kristiane Silkjær, Gl. Færgevej · the father. The entry gives the date of the marriage, ties Niels to Knudsgade 18 in 1931 and hence to the tax book’s entry for 1932, and lists his parents as godparents. Godparent no. 1, the clerk Mette Hansen, has the address Bag Teglværket 8 — the same address the marriage entry of 1930 gives for Ane Kirstine’s parents, the brickworks labourer Jørgen Georg Hansen and his wife [S154]. So she comes from the mother’s home and is in all likelihood her sister, but the kinship is not written out in the entry
S110 The register of Dannebrogsmænd of the Chapter of the Royal Orders, page 510 — “Niels Sielkjær, tjenstgørende Baadmand ved Redningsstationen Vedersø. Udnævnt den 10. November 1915. Begrundelse ej tilgaaet Ordenskapitlet. Levnetsbeskrivelse indsendt.” (Niels Sielkjær, serving boatman at the Vedersø lifeboat station. Appointed on 10 November 1915. Grounds not received by the Chapter. Account of life submitted.) The page carries two later stamps: one about the death in June 1928 and “Dek. indk. 9/7 1928” (decoration received 9/7 1928) — after the death the badge was returned to the Chapter of the Royal Orders, as the rules required. Note the register’s spelling Sielkjær. Copy obtained by the archivist Asbjørn Thyssen Hansen, the Chapter of the Royal Orders, Det Gule Palæ, April 2015, for Helene Silkjær of the Gudum branch — the millwright’s descendants; passed on to the chronicle in 2026
S111 Account of the life of the Dannebrogsmand and boatman Niels Silkjær, submitted to the Chapter of the Royal Orders in November 1915 — two handwritten pages in the first person, the photograph sent with it (reproduced as image 41 — the same exposure as images 14 and 34) and a printed oath of loyalty with the journal numbers Adm-K.C. 1915 and R.P.N. 1083/1915, signed “Vedersø den 30. November 1915, Niels Silkjær”. The quotation in chapter 7 follows the handwriting; a few words are read with uncertainty. Copy as S110
S112 Levy roll, Ringkøbing County, levy district 28 (Husby parish), letter Y — entry in 1873, the calendar year he turned 18 — serial no. 5: “Niels Thomsen”, father the smallholder Thomas Jensen, born Husby 9/7 1855, height 62¾ inches, residence Husby. Endorsement: “1878. Frik. 29½″ Brystmaal. Udsl.” (1878. Exempted. 29½″ chest measurement. Struck off.) — the abbreviated words are not read with complete certainty, but the entry is struck through diagonally, as was done on removal from the roll. Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline. Reproduced as image 42
S113 Confirmation entry 1959, Esbjerg — no. 4: “Annette Hyllested”, parents “Repræsentant Ronald Sören Hyllested og hustru Annagrethe Thomsen” (sales representative Ronald Sören Hyllested and his wife Annagrethe Thomsen), residence Spangsbjerg Kirkevej 42. Birth and baptism traced back to Zion parish: born in May 1944, baptised in July — the baptismal entry is the one that carries the adoption endorsement, cf. S93
S114 Correspondence with the Ulfborg-Vemb Local History Archive, August 2026 — permission to reproduce the archive’s photographs with the form of credit “Foto: [photographer] · Ulfborg-Vemb Lokalhistoriske Arkiv, [archive no.]”; information that Silbjerg and Silkjær are two different farms, and that Silbjerg lies nearer Husby Sø, some way west of Silkjær; confirmation of the district’s custom of calling people by the name of their farm and that with the Names Act of 1905 many officially took a surname after their farm; and a reservation about Wos i æ hawbjerre, whose author, an outsider, according to people with generations in the parish got a number of things wrong
S115 Death certificate (form B), issued by the district medical officer in Lemvig — “Laurits Nikolaj Poulsen”, unmarried, died 28 November 1923 at the county hospital in Lemvig, 28 years old, last permanent residence in Gudum parish; duration of illness 14 days, signs of death rigor, frigor, livores. The cause of death is read as furunculosis with ensuing blood poisoning; the words are partly indistinct, and the birthday and birthplace are uncertain readings. The identification rests on three coincidences with the baptismal entry of 1917, cf. S105: the full form of the name, the age (28 in 1923 corresponds to birth around 1895 — the baptismal entry gives him as 22 in 1917) and the parish of residence, Gudum. Danish National Archives: National Board of Health, Historical Cause-of-Death Register, the series Death Certificates, Jutland — 1923 Ringkøbing rural district, folders 4—12. Reproduced as image 43
S116 The women’s work in the west Jutland fishermen’s huts: Trap Danmark, the article “De vestjyske fiskerboder” (The west Jutland fishermen’s huts) (trap.lex.dk) — the hut was a framed building of turf, reed and marram grass with two double bunks, one for men and the other for women, and the women’s work consisted of coiling the fishing lines, mending, washing and drying them, baiting the hooks, gutting cod and boiling train oil from the livers, as well as cooking and keeping the place clean. Trap Danmark, 5th edition, Holmsland Klit parish (trap5.lex.dk) — the fishermen’s huts in the dunes, where the fishermen and the “esepiger” (bait girls) who put bait on the hooks lived from April until Midsummer. The displays at the Esehusene in Nymindegab put a bait girl’s day’s work at four tubs of 600 hooks each, c. 2,400 in all — the quantity one fisherman could set on one trip — and one bait girl per fisherman
S117 Vridsløselille as an institution in 1913: the house of correction on Vridsløselille Mark (from 1933 Vridsløselille State Prison) was organised on the Philadelphia system — sentences served in solitary confinement day and night, a mask outside the cell, a ban on conversation and stalls in church and school; compulsory masks were only made voluntary in 1924, and the principle of isolation remained central until the Penal Code of 1930, in force in 1933. The Penal Code of 1866 at the same time laid down a reduction of the term for sentences served in solitary confinement — isolation was in itself considered an aggravating element — so that the actual time served by prisoners in the house of correction lay between 6 months and 3½ years, against sentences of 8 months to 6 years; the reduction was maintained until 1933. § 13 of the Act set the reduction at one third for the first three years; eighteen months of hard labour in the house of correction thereby became twelve, which corresponds exactly to the prison register’s date of release (27 April 1914, one year after the start of the sentence). The conversion has been checked against the text of the law; that the sentence was in fact served in solitary confinement is the law’s main rule and an inference from the date, not information in the prison register. The General Civil Penal Code of 10 February 1866, § 13 · Fængselshistorisk Selskab (Prison History Society), faengselshistorie.dk · kilderne.dk, the archive series Vridsløselille State Prison, register 1859—1932 · “Statsfængslet i Vridsløselille — del 1”, Nordisk Tidsskrift for Kriminalvidenskab, vol. 46, no. 4
S118 Correspondence with Museum Vest, August 2026 (head of history and collections) — four photographs of Esbjerg cutters with neutrality markings: E.169 LOLA, E.99 MAAGEN, E.82 NORDSTRAND and E.300 BRITTA (the last photographed by Niels P. Andersen, the other photographers unknown); free use with credit to Museum Vest. The museum also states that its photographs of E.94 are without neutrality markings and not well verified
S119 Police record book 1912—14, Ulfborg-Hind district court (B-080A), vol. 5094 — case 26/13, the hearings of 24 and 28 February (pp. 145, 148—149), 7 March (pp. 153—155), 22 March (p. 174) and 26 March 1913 (p. 177), and the maintenance case 36/13 (pp. 155—156, examination and settlement 7 March). Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed in the reading room on 5 August 2026 and transcribed from the photographs. The key passages — the Hornbeck passage, the Harboøre Fund, “hans første Angreb” (his first attack), the admission “maa siges at have forført hende” (must be said to have seduced her), the withdrawal under § 174 and Enevold Jepsen Enevoldsen as “fødte Værge” (natural guardian) — have been read on full-resolution crops. At the examination on 24 February (p. 145) “fremlagdes under A en Rapport fra Jensen af 17 ds.” (there was produced under A a report from Jensen of the 17th inst.) — the case’s exhibit A is thereby identified directly in the record book. The examination on 24 February was led by the acting deputy H. Gronenberg and the examination on 28 February by the acting deputy Th. Edsberg, both standing in for the ordinary judge — the names and the time of 11.30 on 24 February also appear in the certified transcript in the criminal file, see caveat 28. Pages 153 and 174 reproduced as images 44 and 45
S120 Case list/journal to the police record books 1890—1919, Ulfborg-Hind district court, vols. 5108—5110 — the year 1913: row 26/13 “Sag mod Thomas Nielsen Silkjær for Blodskam” (case against Thomas Nielsen Silkjær for incest), hearing dates 24/2, 28/2, 7/3, 17/3, 22/3 and 26/3, concluded; row 36/13 (the maintenance case) and row 82/1913 “Pat. S. Christine Oline Enevoldsen ctr. Thomas Nielsen Silkjær” (paternity case), brought 18/6, concluded 20/6 1913. Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed 5 August 2026. The case list gives 17 March as a court day — the hearing held at the property at Årgab and entered in the travelling police court book [S163], see caveat 29
S121 Judgment book 1828—1919, Ulfborg-Hind district court, vol. 5140 — the judgment of 14 April 1913 in justice case no. 6/1913, fol. 101—102: the grounds with Kristine Oline’s objections as reported, the admission of seduction (“maa siges at have forført hende til det mellem dem stedfundne usædelige Forhold”, must be said to have seduced her into the immoral relationship that took place between them), the legal basis § 162, in her case taken together with §§ 21 and 37, the verdict “Forbedringshusarbejde i Atten Maaneder” (hard labour in the house of correction for eighteen months, written out in words), the suspended sentence under § 20 of the provisional Penal Code of 1 April 1911 and costs jointly and severally with fees of 30 and 25 kroner. The judge’s signature has not been deciphered. Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed 5 August 2026 and transcribed from the photographs. Fol. 102 reproduced as image 46
S122 Extraordinary court record 1905—1941, the Court in Ringkøbing (Criminal Court), vol. 5487, p. 94 — the trial on 11 April 1913 at 10.30 at the court house (the prosecutor Grove with submission and exhibits; defence counsel Kamp appearing by a substitute with the remark about documents lent “underhaanden”, informally; Thomas brought from the jail; “Tiltalte Christine Oline Enevoldsen mødte ikke efter Paaraab”, the accused Christine Oline Enevoldsen did not appear when called) and the delivery of judgment on 14 April at 4 p.m. at the district office with reference to the judgment book fol. 101. The substitute’s name, “Sagf. Hammersø”, is confirmed by the certified transcript in the criminal file — see caveat 28. Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed 5 August 2026
S123 Police journal 1911—1915 (journal to the police record books), Ringkjøbing town and Ulfborg-Hind Hundreds — journal no. 48/1913, opened 17 February 1913: “Overtrædelse af Strfl. § 162 (Besvangrelse af Steddatter)” (breach of Penal Code § 162, impregnation of a stepdaughter), occasion “Rapp. fra Jensen at Thomas Nielsen Silkjær af Aargab har gjort sig skyldig heri” (report from Jensen that Thomas Nielsen Silkjær of Aargab is guilty of this), and the dispatch column 18/2—3/7: letter to the Copenhagen Police 18/2, telegram in return, correspondence with the parish priest on Holmsland Klit 8/3—10/3, midwife’s certificate from the district midwife A. J. Paulsen 10/3, recommendation to prosecute sent to the county 28/3, order of prosecution returned 31/3, “15/4 til Sfd. Haurvig” returned 22/4, dispatch to Vridsløselille 25/4, a letter from there (“fra do.”) 10/6 and the endorsement “expederes 3/7” — what the individual dispatches contained is not apparent from the journal. The offices of town bailiff and district bailiff were combined, so the journal covers both jurisdictions. Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed 5 August 2026. The row reproduced as image 47
S124 Aarhus St John’s parish register — female births 1913, no. 93: “Else Margrethe Nielsen af Aargab”, born 15 November 1913 at Bethesda, the unmarried Nielsine Nielsen and declared father the fisherman Thomas Nielsen Silkjær; mother and daughter staying with the grandparents, the smallholder Thyge Nielsen and his wife Else Margrethe Nielsen of Aargab, Holmsland Klit; baptised in St John’s Church on 14 December 1913, where among others Johanne Nielsen stood godparent. Nielsine’s date of birth, 23 November 1887, is confirmed by the parish register entry, by the baptismal entry in Nysogn (Haurvig church district), 1887 (S129) and by the census of 1890 (the census of 1930 mistakenly writes 1888). The censuses of 1916 and 1921 list Else Margrethe with her grandparents at Årgab as foster child and child respectively and give the birthday as 13 November — the parish register takes precedence, see caveat 32. The census of 5 November 1930 lists both Nielsine and her daughter in the smallholder Thyge Nielsen’s household at Årgab — the mother unmarried and forty-three, Else Margrethe seventeen. Her documented stay with her grandparents thus runs from 1916 to 1930
S125 Mette Seidelin: “Da børn var medskyldige. Om blodskamssager og lovgivning før 1967” (When children were accomplices: on incest cases and legislation before 1967), Fynske Årbøger 2010 — a review of the incest legislation 1866—1933 and of Statistics Denmark’s figures: on average 26.2 people convicted of incest a year in the years around 1900 (the provision’s peak); around the turn of the century women made up about a third of those convicted in cases under §§ 161—162; after the age of criminal responsibility was raised to 14 in 1906, a total of 15 people between 14 and 18 were punished for incest in the whole country up to 1932; convicted daughters typically received eight months to a year in the house of correction, up to two years, and daughters whose “morality” was called into question were sentenced most harshly. Only the Penal Code of 1930 (in force 1933) exempted the children
S126 Statistical Yearbook 1908, Statistics Denmark — the table of convictions by type of offence: incest, 12—18 people convicted a year nationally 1903—07. The statistics count people, not cases; in cases under § 162 where both parties were convicted, the man and the girl count as two convicted persons
S127 The General Civil Penal Code of 10 February 1866 — § 162: sexual intercourse with a stepchild, penal servitude of up to 6 years for the step-parent; for the stepchild, in mitigating circumstances, imprisonment, “ikke under 2 Maaneders simpelt Fængsel” (not less than 2 months’ simple imprisonment); § 174: seduction of a girl between 12 and 16 into fornication, prosecutable only at the request of the parents or guardian; § 21: persons under 18 could not be sentenced to imprisonment on bread and water; § 37: for persons between 15 and 18 the statutory penalty was reduced “efter Omstændighederne indtil det Halve” (according to circumstances by up to half). Suspended sentences: introduced by the provisional Penal Code of 1 April 1905, continued by the provisional Penal Code of 1 April 1911, whose § 20 is the provision cited by the judgment of 14 April 1913
S128 Bethesda in Aarhus: AarhusWiki, the entry “Bethesda” — a rescue and maternity home for unmarried pregnant women, founded in 1894 as an offshoot of the Magdalene Asylum with a deaconess as matron, aimed at “den første Gang faldne Pige” (the girl fallen for the first time); from 21 October 1897 in premises on Aarhus Mark by Skovvangsvej with room for 20 women and 30 children; from 1901 under the Magdalene Home in Copenhagen as the Bethesda Rescue and Maternity Home; moved only in November 1923 to Bethesdavej. Its running rested mainly on funds from the Inner Mission until the social reform of 1933. In November 1913 the home lay by Skovvangsvej in St John’s parish — hence the birth entry and the baptism in St John’s Church
S129 Nysogn (Haurvig church district) — female births 1887, no. 11: Nielsine Nielsen, born 23 November 1887, baptised 4 December 1887 in Haurvig Church, daughter of the smallholder Tyge Nielsen and his wife Else Magrete Pedersen (30 years) of Aargab. The baptismal entry documents the date of birth, the birthplace and the mother’s name — the grandmother after whom Else Margrethe was named in 1913, cf. S124
S130 Postcard from Jens Klaus Silkjær, Øster Alling Præstegaard, to “Frk. Kirstine Silkjær, Husby Præstegaard pr Ulfborg”, dated 18 April 1911 and postmarked in Auning; the front is a photograph of the tenant family and servants in front of the rectory farm — private collection, the Silkjær family. Transcription made for this chronicle from a photographic copy
S131 Studio photograph of Jens Klaus Silkjær’s six sons, c. 1926—27, with the names Johannes, Henry, Verner, Tage, Oluf and Niels written in the margin — private collection, the Silkjær family
S132 Death certificate issued by a doctor, form B.1 (Danish National Archives, death certificates) — “Else Margrethe Nielsen. Ugift.” (unmarried), born 15/11 1913 in Aarhus, occupation domestic help, last permanent residence Hvide Sande, population-register municipality Nysogn, Ringkøbing medical district. Place of death: the Mental Hospital in Viborg; date of death 10 November 1938 at 7 p.m. Principal illness given as bronchopneumonia with morbus mentalis; immediate cause of death “Lungebetændelse” (pneumonia) / bronchopneumonia. The certificate issued in Viborg on 11 November 1938 by the hospital’s doctor. At the top of the form: Nørre Haurvig churchyard. Birthday and birthplace correspond to the parish register entry in Aarhus St John’s 1913 [S124], and the certificate thus settles both her civil status and her death
S133 Census of 1 February 1916, Esbjerg, Vor Frelsers parish — Nørregade 44: Kristine Oline Enevoldsen, born 17 May 1896, unmarried, servant girl, occupation domestic help, in the household of Anders Hansen Larsen and Anne Marie Larsen, their children and a lodger (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline)
S134 Sigurd Enggaard Poulsen, “Landet bag hav — omkring en fjord” (The land behind the sea — around a fjord), Poul Kristensen, Herning 1977 (Danskernes Historie Online, slaegtsbibliotek.dk/937115.pdf). Christen Christensen Sørensen, known as “Kræ Krænsen” (b. Årgab 1857, grew up at Hummelbu south of Revsgård, from 1880 at Nr. Bork Fælled, moved to Skjern 1928), memoirs written down in 1931 — the prayer at the launching of the sea boat and the passing of the quiet moment pp. 199—200, Christmas in the childhood home pp. 177—178, the defeats after the conversion pp. 191—192, biographical data pp. 141—143. Conversations with his daughter Oline “Line” Holm (c. 1885 — 1 February 1977) pp. 191—192 — the priest’s ball, her mother’s diphtheria and the home’s conversion in 1901, her uncle Chr. Sørensen’s letters from Årgab, her father’s later relapse. Anders Poulsen, Nr. Bork, on the returned pack of cards pp. 182—183. The account of the wreck and the drownings of 20.5.1894 and 1.4.1896 with the thirteen dead pp. 201—202, given by the author as “et resumé af omtalen i Ringkøbing Amts Dagblad” (a summary of the report in Ringkøbing Amts Dagblad)
S135 P. Pedersen, “Klittens historie” (The history of the dunes), quoted from Poulsen 1977 p. 200 — H.P. Kristensen, dune dweller and later priest (emeritus in Silkeborg), on his mother’s Christmas Eve prayer and evening prayer, the hymns, the book of sermons, the North Sea as “den anden præst” (the other priest) and the modesty that kept mouths shut. Given at two removes; the original has not been seen
S136 Sønder Nissum parish register, marriages 6 December 1940, no. 8 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — “Ungkarl, Fisker af Sdr. Nissum Sogn Niels Poulsen, født i Husby Sogn, Ulfborg Herred, 1917, 28. April. Søn af Jensine Kristine Nielsen Silkjær og Tjenestekarl Laurits Nikolaj Poulsen. Moderen nu gift med Husmand i Fjand Martin Jeppesen Nørfjand” (bachelor, fisherman of Sdr. Nissum parish, Niels Poulsen, born in Husby parish, Ulfborg Hundred, 28 April 1917; son of Jensine Kristine Nielsen Silkjær and the farmhand Laurits Nikolaj Poulsen; the mother now married to the smallholder in Fjand Martin Jeppesen Nørfjand) — married to “Pige, Husassistent af Sdr. Nissum Sogn Maria Nielsen, født i Arnborg Sogn, Hammerum Herred, 1919, 22. December, Datter af Elisabeth Jensen og Tjenestekarl Kristian Nielsen” (the girl Maria Nielsen, domestic help of Sdr. Nissum parish, born in Arnborg parish, Hammerum Hundred, 22 December 1919, daughter of Elisabeth Jensen and the farmhand Kristian Nielsen). Banns read on 16 and 17 November 1940; married in church by the parish priest. Witnesses: “Mødrene” (the mothers). The parish bailiff of Sdr. Nissum, certificate of 16 November. The entry confirms the birthday 28 April 1917 against the census’s 29th. The couple’s three children according to the family transcript on 1uz.dk [S1]
S137 Studio photograph of three sisters from Økjær — Ane Kirstine (left), Karen Marie (centre) and Sidsel Kathrine (right) — c. 1910—15 according to the family’s album inscription; private collection, the Silkjær family. Reproduced as image 52
S138 Studio portrait of Kristian Kornelius Bøndergaard (1888—1955), married to Karen Marie Nielsen Silkjær on 18 September 1913 in Husby Church — private collection, the Silkjær family. Reproduced as image 53
S139 Esbjerg civil marriage register, p. 12 (Danish National Archives) — civil marriage on 2 December 1950 at 12.10 between “Arne Enevoldsen”, accountant, born 26 May 1913 at Aargab, Holmsland Klit, and “Edna Alice Söderwall født Gram”, telephonist, born 21 September 1913 in Esbjerg. Both entered as divorced and married once before; both residing at Strandbygade 39, Esbjerg. Witnesses: the municipal assistant Miss F. Halkjær-Lassen and the office assistant Mrs Ellen Thyggesen. Certificate from the Esbjerg Mayor’s Office of 13 November 1950; the marriage conducted by L. M. Nielsen. The same register, p. 52: Ronald Søren Hyllested, police constable, Jernbanegade 2, and Annagrethe Enevoldsen, née Thomsen, office assistant, Kirkegade 101, born 4 April 1916 in Jerne parish — both entered as divorced by licence, she on 3 June 1949, he on 27 July 1949 — married by the Copenhagen Magistrates on 11 February 1950; transcript received in Esbjerg on 14 February. The two entries date Arne’s divorce, his second marriage and Annagrethe’s
S140 Esbjerg Fiskeriforening 1892—1942 (Esbjerg Fishermen’s Association), anniversary publication (perbenny.dk) — the bank clerk E. Enevoldsen had for many years been treasurer and bookkeeper of the fishermen’s liability insurance; after his death the work was handed over to the accountant Arne Enevoldsen
S141 Registreringstidende for Aktieselskaber, Forsikringsselskaber og Foreninger (the register gazette for companies, insurers and associations), 5 January 1945 (tidsskrift.dk) — Register number 468, “Ansvarsforsikringen for Esbjerg Fiskere, gensidigt Selskab med begrænset Ansvar” (the Esbjerg Fishermen’s Liability Insurance, mutual society with limited liability), liability insurance for owners and masters of fishing vessels in the Esbjerg customs district, articles of 7 March 1914 with amendments most recently of 22 December 1943, approved 17 August 1944. Board: fishing skipper Christian Enevold Sørensen (chairman), fishing skipper Søren Andreas Jensen, fishing skipper Anton Kristensen, fishing skipper Thomas Silkjær and fishing skipper Peder Heide, all of Esbjerg. Manager: Arne Enevoldsen, Esbjerg. “Foreningen tegnes af Bestyrelsens Formand i Forening med et Medlem af Bestyrelsen eller med Forretningsføreren.” (The society is bound by the chairman of the board together with a member of the board or with the manager.) Notices to members appear in the daily Vestkysten
S142 Death certificate for Sidsel Kathrine Nielsen Silkjær and Esbjerg’s burial register. Death certificate issued by a doctor, form B.1 (Danish National Archives, death certificates), no. 14 — “Sidsel Kathrine Nielsen Silkjær”, unmarried, born 24 December 1894 in Husby. The columns “Bopæl (sidste faste Opholdssted)” (residence, last permanent address) and “Dødsstedet” (place of death) are filled in with the same address, Havnegade 152 in Esbjerg — so she died at her home address and not in a hospital. The certificate does not say whether the home was her own or whether she lived with others. The floor is given but difficult to decipher. The details of the grave come not from the certificate but from Esbjerg’s burial register: buried 26 May 1938 in the churchyard in Gormsgade, section R, row 13, nos. 17—18; the grave renewed until 1958. Date of death 18 May 1938 at 6 p.m. Principal illness: tuberculosis pulmonum; immediate cause of death given as “Lungetuberkulose” / tb. pulmonum. Certain signs of death: rigor mortis and livor mortis. The certificate issued in Esbjerg on 19 May 1938 by Dr T. Jensen. The occupation column reads “Fhv. Sygeplejerske” (former nurse). The certificate does not say when or why she stopped working, and does not connect the illness with her profession
S143 Esbjerg’s burial registers, day journal 16 June 1936 — 15 October 1948, vol. 14 (transcribed, Esbjerg City Archives, id 48323) — surname “Thomsen”, first names “Ane kaldet Silkjær” (Ane called Silkjær), 78 years, died 28 June 1936, buried 3 July 1936 in Gormsgade, section Ø, row 11, no. 10, the grave renewed until 31 December 1956. The grave lies beside Ø-11-9, where her son Thomas was buried in 1950 and Kristiane in 1963 [S108]. The journal’s date of death differs from the family file’s 23 June; the difference has not been resolved
S144 Death certificate issued by a doctor, form B.1, no. 22 (Danish National Archives, death certificates) — “Ane Silkjær f. Jensen”, widow, born 29 April 1858 in Ejsing parish, entered as “enke efter husmand og fisker, aldersrentenyder” (widow of a smallholder and fisherman, old-age pensioner). Residence and place of death: Havnegade 179, Esbjerg. Date of death 28 June 1936 at 3 a.m. Principal illness: arteriosclerosis and myocarditis with insufficientia cordis; immediate cause of death given as “Hjertelammelse” (heart failure) / insufficientia cordis. Certain signs of death: rigor mortis and livores. The body examined on 28 June at 10.30 by Dr I. Diehl, Kongensgade 87, Esbjerg, who issued the certificate the same day. The certificate settles the date of death against the family file’s 23 June
S145 Esbjerg Municipality, wealth and lodging taxes 1927—1928, vol. 5, the list of taxpayers who moved away or died 1900—1928 (transcribed, Esbjerg City Archives, id 33711) — “Sidsel Cathrine Nielsen Silkjær”, occupation “oversygeplejerske” (head nurse), address Gl. Færgevej 7. Date of departure 1 December 1927, moved to Læborg, address unknown, with the note “Hos: Vognmand Poul Christensen” (with the haulier Poul Christensen).
S146 Census of 5 November 1930, Læborg parish (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — Sidsel Kathrine Nielsen Silkjær is still living in the parish almost three years after moving there, but no longer as a lodger: she has her own household. The form number and address were not noted when the entry was consulted. The time of her return to Esbjerg has not been established
S147 Death notice for Arne Enevoldsen, newspaper cutting in the family’s possession — “Vor kære og elskede Arne Enevoldsen er stille sovet ind, Vejle, den 27. december 1998. På familiens vegne, Edna Enevoldsen. Begravelsen har fundet sted.” (Our dear and beloved Arne Enevoldsen has quietly fallen asleep, Vejle, 27 December 1998. On behalf of the family, Edna Enevoldsen. The funeral has taken place.) The notice establishes the date of death and ties the death to Vejle; it also shows that Edna survived him. It does not document when the couple left Esbjerg or where they lived in the years before
S148 Genealogical record of Esper Nielsen Silkjær’s family — extract from a table of descendants, compiled around 2009 (it refers to two of the children as “endnu lever (2009)”, still living in 2009), received August 2026. It gives the marriage on 17 March 1913 in Gudum, the farm Nørre Tangshus as the home of the couple and the children, their old age at Fredensgade 11 in Struer and eight children with dates of birth and baptism from the Gudum parish register; the entries have not been checked in the original. On Knud Vognsgaard: employed on 26 April 1953 as a smelter at the steelworks in Frederiksværk, killed in the explosion there on 27 May 1959, buried on 31 May in Skævinge; married to Ebba Ruth Nielsen, left a wife and three children — the disaster is independently confirmed by the obituary in the folk high school’s alumni magazine [S149] and by Halsnæs Municipality’s cultural heritage analysis [S150]; press reports and the death certificate have not been traced, and the course of events itself has not been reconstructed. The family file [S40] spells the middle name Vagnsgaard, where the record writes Vognsgaard; the parish register has not been consulted. Of Alma the record writes “aldrig gift” (never married), while the family file lists a marriage — the contradiction has not been resolved, and the chronicle takes no position. The children’s years and places of death (Niels 1999 in Struer, Krista 2006 in a care home on Amager, Alma 2013 at Svendborg hospital, Helga 2004 in Arnborg — the record says Herning, near which Arnborg lies) follow the family file; Otto’s emigration to Australia and his death rest on the record alone
S149 Nr. Nissum Folk High School alumni magazine, no. 6, June 1959 (skolehistorie.dk) — obituary of Knud Vognsgaard Silkjær, winter student 1933/34, with a portrait photograph, reproduced as image 54. Written by his sister, who signs “Ane Pedersen, f. Silkjær (1938)” — herself a former student; the signature independently confirms the record’s [S148] marriage between Ane Kristiane and Thorvald Pedersen. The text opens “Onsdag den 27. maj fik vi det tunge budskab, at vor kære broder Knud var død som følge af den store ulykke på Frederiksværk Stålvalseværk” (On Wednesday 27 May we received the heavy news that our dear brother Knud had died as a result of the great disaster at the Frederiksværk steelworks) — 27 May 1959 was a Wednesday — and records a wife and three children aged 19, 16 and 8, “et dejligt hus med have” (a lovely house with a garden) in Skævinge, the daily drive to the works in Frederiksværk and the family’s last meeting with him at Easter, “da han var hjemme i Struer med familien” (when he was at home in Struer with the family) — with his parents Esper and Jensine, cf. S148. The school’s own addition: “Han var så ung og så glad og fornøjelig. Havde vi ikke haft ham på vinterholdet for 25 år siden, så havde der ligesom manglet noget væsentligt.” (He was so young and so cheerful and good company. Had we not had him in the winter class 25 years ago, something essential would have been missing.) The magazine spells the town “Skævingen”. Nørre Nissum Folk High School was the Inner Mission’s first folk high school in Denmark, founded in 1887 by the parish priest Ad. L. Hansen in collaboration with the Inner Mission’s board and Vilhelm Beck — cf. the school’s anniversary publications of 1937, 1962 and 1987, in the same place
S150 Analysis of Frederiksværk’s industrial heritage — preliminary analysis for Stålsat By (Steel-set Town), Halsnæs Municipality (halsnaes.dk) — on Det Danske Staalvalseværk: “Det var ikke nogen sikker arbejdsplads. I 1959 mistede fem arbejdere livet og mange andre fik skader for livet, efter en stor eksplosion.” (It was not a safe workplace. In 1959 five workers lost their lives and many others were injured for life after a great explosion.) The same analysis sets out the scale of the works in the 1950s: almost 1,000 employees and an annual steel production of 110,000 tons, the country’s largest recycling plant. The analysis does not date the explosion more closely; the day, 27 May, comes from the genealogical record [S148] and is confirmed by the alumni magazine [S149]
S151 Census of 5 November 1940, Esbjerg, Havnegade (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — Anna Silkjær, born 17 February 1907, at no. 179, and Anna Kirstine Silkjær Torbensen, born 15 April 1929, at no. 132 in her parents’ household. The census separates the two namesakes in the same street and confirms that the godparent at the baptism in Zion’s Church in April 1945 — “frøken ekspeditrice Anna Silkjær, Havnegade 179” (Miss Anna Silkjær, shop assistant) — is Thomas Nielsen Silkjær’s daughter and not his niece
S152 Photographs from the family’s own collection, received in August 2026 through Helene Silkjær; the files carry the watermark of the family tree “Silkjaer Dynastiet” on MyHeritage. Three of them are reproduced in chapter 20: the bridal couple Esper and Jensine, an undated family gathering in Gudum and a christening at Anne Kristiane’s in Hjerm. None of the three bears an inscription, photographer’s stamp or date, and the identifications rest solely on the names the family has given the files. The year of marriage, 1913, and the farm Nørre Tangshus agree with the record of descendants [S148], but the photograph itself is linked to the wedding only by family tradition
S153 The National Museum of Denmark, history of fashion, “Hvid brudekjole — chemisekjole ca. 1797” (White wedding dress — chemise dress c. 1797) (natmus.dk): “Blandt bønder og den jævne del af bybefolkningen har sort brudekjole været det mest almindelige. Det var ikke kun et spørgsmål om økonomi, men også om tradition” (among farmers and the ordinary part of the town population the black wedding dress was the most common; it was not only a question of money but also of tradition) — white was for “de fine” (the gentry). Magasin du Nord Museum, the exhibition “Det er så yndigt”: in the nineteenth century most Danish brides were married in a simple black dress, sewn for the occasion, which would afterwards serve as the best party dress; only around 1920 did white become the dominant colour for wedding dresses
S154 Vor Frelser parish register, Esbjerg, marriages 21 December 1930, no. 21 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — “Ungk. Fisker, Gl. Færgevej 7, Esbjerg, Niels Silkjær, f. 26. September 1910 i Aargab, Holmslands Klit, søn af fiskeskipper Thomas Nielsen Silkjær og hustru Christiane Enevoldsen, Gl. Færgevej 7” (bachelor, fisherman, Gl. Færgevej 7, Esbjerg, Niels Silkjær, b. 26 September 1910 at Aargab, Holmsland Klit, son of the fishing skipper Thomas Nielsen Silkjær and his wife Christiane Enevoldsen), married to “Ugift Husassistent, Bag Teglværket 8, Esbjerg, Ane Kirstine Hansen, f. 10. September 1910, Vor Frelsers Sogn, Esbjerg, datter af teglværksarbejder Jørgen Georg Hansen og hustru Ane Margrethe Kristensen Holm, Bag Teglværket 8” (unmarried domestic help, Bag Teglværket 8, Esbjerg, Ane Kirstine Hansen, b. 10 September 1910, Vor Frelsers parish, Esbjerg, daughter of the brickworks labourer Jørgen Georg Hansen and his wife Ane Margrethe Kristensen Holm). Banns read on 4, 7 and 8 December 1930; married in Vor Frelsers Church by Pastor P. Iversen. Certificate from the Mayor’s Office of 4 December 1930, no. 344. The entry names Ane Kirstine’s parents and explains their son’s first names: he was named after his maternal grandfather. The godparent at the son’s baptism in 1931, the clerk Mette Hansen, Bag Teglværket 8, comes from the same household [S109]
S155 Zion parish register, Esbjerg, births 1940, no. 74 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — Elisabeth Silkjær, born 6 July 1940 at the Municipal Hospital, residence Gormsgade 122. Parents: the fisherman Niels Silkjær, b. 26 September 1910, and his wife Ane Kirstine Hansen, b. 10 September 1910, married in Vor Frelser Church on 21 December 1930. Baptised at home on 17 July by Pastor Bentzen and presented in Zion’s Church on 15 September 1940. Witnesses at the presentation: the fishing skipper Thomas Silkjær and his wife Christiane, Havnegade 179, and the labourer Georg Hansen and his wife Maren, Grønnegade 29. The entry confirms the household at Gormsgade 122 and the marriage date in 1930 [S154]. Note that the marriage entry of 1930 lists Ane Kirstine’s mother as Ane Margrethe Kristensen Holm, Bag Teglværket 8, while the baptism of 1940 lists Georg Hansen’s wife as Maren, Grønnegade 29; whether this is the same woman under two forms of name or a new marriage has not been clarified.
S156 Esbjerg’s burial registers, day journal 1989—1998, vol. 54 (transcribed, Esbjerg City Archives, id 32958) — surname Jensen, first name Elisabeth, née Silkjær, born 6 July 1940, died 17 November 1997, buried 21 November in Gormsgade, section R, row 62, no. 5, the grave renewed until 31 December 2007. Notes: “D.D.”, cremated 25 November, interred 28 November 1997. The date of birth corresponds to the parish register entry [S155], and the maiden name confirms that she is Niels Silkjær’s daughter from Gormsgade 122
S157 Zion parish register, Esbjerg, births 1950 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — Thomas Silkjær Nielsen, born 19 February 1950 in Esbjerg, residence Spangsberggade 44, 2nd floor. Parents: the forwarding agent Holger Nielsen, b. 5 June 1919, and his wife Elna Elisabeth Silkjær, b. 20 January 1919, married in Zion’s Church on 10 October 1942. Baptised in church on 6 April 1950 by Pastor K. Brask. Godparents: 1—2. the child’s parents · 3. Miss Anna Silkjær, Havnegade 179 · 4. fishing skipper Niels Silkjær, Strandbygade 67 · 5. fisherman Kristian Silkjær, Havnegade 179. The entry dates the father’s change from clerk to forwarding agent, confirms the marriage of 1942 [S101] and brings together three of Thomas Nielsen Silkjær’s children as godparents seventeen days after his death. He himself died on 20 March 1950 [S108]
S158 Mogens Silkjær Nielsen (16.6.1951—9.12.1997). Zion parish register, Esbjerg, births 1951 — born 16 June 1951, residence Spangsberggade 44, 1st floor; parents the forwarding agent Holger Nielsen, b. 5 June 1919, and his wife Elna Elisabeth Silkjær, b. 20 January 1919, married in Zion’s Church on 10 October 1942. Baptised in church on 12 August 1951 by Pastor K. Brask; godparents the coal merchant Karl Jensen and his wife Esther, Kronprinsensgade 25, and the child’s parents. Esbjerg’s burial registers, day journal 1989—1998, vol. 54 (Esbjerg City Archives, id 32978) — surname Silkjær, first name Mogens, born 16 June 1951, died 9 December 1997, buried 13 December in Gormsgade, section K, row 13, no. 69. The register lists him under the surname Silkjær, without Nielsen. Named in full as a journalist at Esbjerg Ugeavis, ugeavisen.dk/esbjerg/jeg-var-ikke-fan-af-gasolin-dengang
S159 Sædding parish register, Bølling Hundred, births 1917 (Danish National Archives, Arkivalieronline) — Laura Madsen, born 25 March 1917 at Rækker Mølle, daughter of the master mason Mads Erik Madsen and his wife Ane Johanne. The original entry confirms date of birth, birthplace and parents; the index [S6] had already pointed to this
S160 Family tree of Ellen Nielsen Silkjær and Peder Christian Burkarl, supplied in August 2026 — shows the couple with nine children, seven of them named: Niels Kristian, Evald, Knud Peder, Karoline Kjærstine, Anne, Anna and Oda. All seven are listed with the name form Silkjær Burkarl. Two children are not identified in the extract available
S161 Census of 1 February 1916, Husby parish — the household of Ane Marie/Ole Lauridsen; Margrethe Dorthea Lauridsen, born 2 September 1908, is listed as daughter
S162 Census of 1 February 1921, Husby parish — Ane Marie Lauridsen’s household; Ole Lauridsen, born 14 May 1916, is listed as son
S163 Travelling police court book 1874—1918, Ulfborg-Hind district court (5104A—C), pp. 72—74 — the police court sitting at Thomas Silkjær’s property at Årgab, Holmsland Klit, on 17 March 1913 at 3.30 p.m., conducted by the ordinary judge with two court witnesses called in: Kristine Oline Enevoldsen’s affirmation of her statement in report A and her detailed statement, with the witness signatures “Enev. J. Enevoldsen” and “Chr. Silkær”. Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed in the reading room on 12 August 2026 and transcribed from the photographs. Page 72 reproduced as image 58. See caveat 29
S164 Documents to the justice records 1766—1919, Ulfborg-Hind district court (5064), 1913 — the draft judgment in justice case no. 6/1913, endorsed “Paadømt 14/4 1913” (adjudged 14/4 1913) and “Indført i Herredernes Domprotokol Fol. 101” (entered in the Hundreds’ judgment book fol. 101), with the corrections visible: the marginal addition “for Tilt.s Vedkommende sammenholdt med §§ 21 og 37” (in the accused’s case taken together with §§ 21 and 37) with an insertion mark, and the struck-through joint sentence, in which Christine Oline Enevoldsen’s name is deleted and she is given a sentence of her own with the suspension. Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed 12 August 2026
S165 Day journal 1880—1932, Ringkjøbing County (5098), 1913 — case D 698: “Thomas Nielsen Silkjær og Christine Oline Enevoldsen — Overtr. af Strfls. § 162” (breach of Penal Code § 162), received from the district office on 28 March 1913; the dispatches 31/3 (prosecution), 22/4—24/4 (judgment received, execution), 5/7—8/7 (the petition for pardon forwarded to the Director of Prisons), 17/7—19/7 (the Ministry of Justice’s reply) and an exchange with the district office 26/9—4/10 whose content is not apparent. Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed 12 August 2026
S166 Case files 1900—1932, Ringkjøbing County (6539), 1913 D — case D 698/1913: the district office’s recommendation to prosecute of 28 March 1913 (“… skal jeg tjenstlig indstille, at de pågældende sættes under Tiltale for Overtrædelse af Straffelovens § 162”, I have the honour officially to recommend that the persons concerned be charged with breach of § 162 of the Penal Code) with the county’s endorsements — 31/3 prosecution and “Arrestantsag” (prisoner case), 24/4 “acquiescerer” and execution, 8/7 the forwarding of the petition for pardon “idet bem., at Amtet kan henholde sig til den af Pol. afgivne Erklæring” — and the Ministry of Justice’s refusal of 17 July 1913, letter no. 2513, journal no. 1026/13. Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed 12 August 2026. The refusal reproduced as image 59
S167 Journal 1859—1943, Vridsløselille State Prison (vols. 77—80, 1910—1919) — the entries on the refusal of the petition for pardon for prisoner no. 240 (forwarded by the Director of Prisons 17—19 July 1913) and on the recommendation on 10 November 1913 of seven prisoners for pardon on the occasion of the fiftieth anniversary of the House of Glücksburg’s reign, with the endorsement “15/11-13 Dir. medd. Kgl. R. af 15/11 13: alle syv benaadede … Alle løsl. 15/11 13” (15/11-13 the Director reports royal resolution of 15/11 13: all seven pardoned … all released 15/11 13). Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed 12 August 2026
S168 Letter book 1859—1943, Vridsløselille State Prison (vols. 7—8, 1912—1920) — letter no. 131 of 10 November 1913 to the Director of Prisons: the recommendation of seven prisoners for the jubilee pardon, among them “No 240 Fisker Thomas Nielsen Silkjær” with the characterisation “Han opfører sig godt og synes at angre sin Forbrydelse. I Hjemmet savnes han haardt” (He conducts himself well and seems to repent of his crime. He is sorely missed at home) and the reference to the judge’s recommendation of the petition refused in July. Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed 12 August 2026
S169 Niels Iversen Klit, “Husby Klit — en egnsskildring fra gammel tid” (Husby Klit — a local account from olden times), no. 8 — summary of the parish board meeting at Husby rectory on 15 April 1846: Jens Claus Mattzen, for whom discharge from school was requested, was examined in arithmetic with a satisfactory result, and the discharge was granted; the request had been submitted too late and should have been made immediately after the autumn examination. The booklet adds that the foreign-looking spelling of the surname was probably due to Jens Claus having been born and baptised in Angeln in South Schleswig. The booklet is probably based on the parish board’s minute book
S170 Parish register for Nysogn (Haurvig church district), births 1893, no. 10 — Søren Mathiasen Pedersen Heide, born 17 November 1893 at Bjerregaard, son of the smallholder Anders Hejde Pedersen and his wife Edel Kirstine Hansen, 27, Bjerregaard; baptised in Haurvig Church on Boxing Day by Pastor Alfred Jørgensen, the mother carrying the child herself, godparents the smallholders Peder Lodbjerg, Laust Kristensen and Søren Thomas Hansen, all of Bjerregaard. “Heide” in the child’s name is in paler ink and was added later: the family received Heide as an official surname by licence of 21 August 1905
S171 Ringkøbing town bailiff: case files (1913) — Ringkjøbing County’s letter of 31 March 1913 from Rindumgaard, the county’s case number D 698 with a printed request that the number be given in letters concerning the case, and the endorsement “Arrestantsag” (prisoner case): in connection with the transcript of examinations received with the chief of police’s letter of the 28th of the same month, notice is given that proceedings were brought the same day against Thomas Nielsen Silkjær and Christine Oline Enevoldsen for breach of § 162 of the Penal Code, and that the barrister Grove and the solicitor Kamp have been appointed to conduct the case, “den førstnævnte som Aktor, den sidstnævnte som Defensor” (the former as prosecutor, the latter as defence counsel); the defence is asked to be given the necessary notice of the above. Signed by the county governor — H.C. Dons, governor of Ringkjøbing County 1903—15, residing at Rindumgaard, cf. Kraks Vejviser 1913. At the bottom the district office’s red journal endorsement 48/13; the offices of town bailiff and district bailiff were combined. Danish National Archives, Viborg; photographed 13 August 2026. Reproduced as image 60
S172 St Michael’s Church, Fredericia — the biography of Carl Marius Hornbech (1871—1934) on the board of priests, compiled by the historical consultant Ole Dyrn (sctm.dk): a priest’s son, schooled at Randers Latin School, cand.theol. 1896, YMCA secretary in Aarhus 1898, ordained assistant in Copenhagen 1899, missionary in India from 1902 — where his first wife Olga died in 1908 — travelling preacher for the Danish Missionary Society from 1909 and parish priest in Fredericia St Michael-Erritsø 1915—34. Supplemented by Dansk Forfatterleksikon (danskforfatterleksikon.dk) and by the school programmes for the preparatory school to the State School in Randers 1912—14 (skolehistorie.dk), which list among the pupils a child with the father given as “Hornbech (Præst)” — so a Pastor Hornbech with children at school lived in Randers in exactly those years
S173 Information given to the chronicle by Annette’s family, August 2026 — on the adoption, the nursing training, the move to Copenhagen during her training, the two children, the presumed absence of contact with her biological father and her death in 2024, shortly after her eightieth birthday, which was celebrated with the family in her daughter’s garden. The informant is known to the chronicle but is not named
S174 The criminal file in the case against Thomas Nielsen Silkjær and Christine Oline Enevoldsen — Ringkøbing Police, box B-410, folder no. 408: “Aktor, Overretssagfører Grove ctr. Thomas Nielsen Silkjær og Christine Oline Enevoldsen”, county journal no. D 698 – 1913. Contents: the transcript of the judgment book “in forma” with endorsements of service and execution; Grove’s summons of 1 April and submission of 2 April 1913; Kamp’s submission of 3 April 1913; a certified transcript of the examinations in the police record book (24 and 28 February, 7, 17, 22 and 26 March) with the county’s order of prosecution of 31 March; and exhibits A—K: the police report of 17 February (A), the arrest requisition of 18 February (B), the transcript of the Copenhagen Criminal and Police Court’s examination no. 575 of 21 February (C), the telegram about the arrest (D), certificates of baptism for Thomas and Christine (E, F), the marriage certificate (G), the midwife’s certificate of 10 March (H) and the certificates of criminal record (I, K). Danish National Archives; photographs received and transcribed on 26 August 2026. See caveat 28
S175 Politiets Efterretninger (the Police Gazette) 1913, no. 23 (22 February) and no. 24 (25 February) — the arrest of Thomas Nielsen Silkjær (Husby, 10/1 82) for breach of § 162 of the Penal Code in another jurisdiction, listed under “Anholdte for Forbrydelser m. v.” (arrested for crimes etc.), and the transfer under “Afgivne til frem. Jurisd.” (handed over to other jurisdictions) with the entry “Til Ulfborg-Hind Herreder” (to Ulfborg-Hind Hundreds). Copenhagen City Archives, transcribed sources — kbharkiv.dk, entries 19-10363 and 19-10380
S176 Politiets Efterretninger 1915, no. 12 (28 January) — Thomas Nielsen Silkjær (Husby, 10/1,82) listed under the heading “Efterlyste Alimentanter” (persons sought for maintenance payments), the day before his son Ejlerth Marius was born in Esbjerg. Copenhagen City Archives, transcribed sources — kbharkiv.dk, entry 19-10723
S177 Torben Klinting, “Fiskerne fra Nymindegab” (The fishermen of Nymindegab) — the account of the disaster of 1 April 1896: the five names of the boat’s crew with position and civil status, the ownership of “Forsøget” and the two young farmhands’ wages, the putting out on the afternoon of 31 March, the course of the wreck, Søren Andersen Jensen drifting on an oar and his rescue by Enevold Enevoldsen with a line round his waist, Peder Enevoldsen drifting on a stump of mast, the beach bailiff Jens Dahl’s finding of the three bodies off Gødelen on Maundy Thursday, the funerals in Haurvig, Nr. Lyngvig and Sdr. Bork, the stranding of the wreck off Hovstrup, the rescue medal to Enevold Enevoldsen and the inscription on the memorial stone. Received as a transcript on 7 September 2026 from Hardy Sørensen, the Archive in Fiskeriets Hus, Hvide Sande; page number not given, the book not seen. See caveat 41
S178 Dagens Nyheder, 28 May 1896, “Mindestøtte over druknede Fiskere” (Memorial to drowned fishermen) — reported from Ringkjøbing Avis: the unveiling of the memorial stone on Whit Sunday, the stone’s place close to the road in Aargab village on a fenced plot given by Knud Andersen, the inscription with the four names, c. 500 present, the gunboat “Grønsund” with its commander Captain Brædstrup and First Lieutenant Reinhardt, “Dejlig er Jorden” (Fair is the Earth) at 3 o’clock and the handing over of the stone from the fishermen of Esbjerg to those of the dunes. Received as a transcript on 7 September 2026 from Hardy Sørensen; the newspaper page has not been seen, and the quotation is given in the transcript’s spelling
S179 Søren Rinder Kristensen, Årgab, account of Ane Marie Enevoldsen (1868—1953) — Peder Enevoldsen’s widow, the children Jensigne (b. 1893) and Kresten, the house at Årgab, her son’s drowning in Ringkøbing Fjord in March 1918 together with Peder Sand and Ole Madsen, her old age with her daughter in Alslev and the grave in Haurvig churchyard. Written down by the author, with additions from Hardy Sørensen. The author is the grandson of the survivor Søren Andersen Jensen and gives the family tradition that his grandfather was saved on an oar. Family tradition, not archival records. See caveat 43
S180 Vragwiki, “Holmsland Klit” (vragwiki.dk) — the list of beach sections on Holmsland Klit, for Bjerregård: 1847 Jens Sørensen, Gl. Bjerregård; 1860—61 Aanders Heide; 1885—89 P.C. Nielsen (Dahl); 1897—1917 Klaus Kr. Nielsen; 1917 Jeppe Klausen and Chr. Rauhe and Chr. Kirk. The years indicate when the names are documented, not terms of office
